'''Peter Zoller''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 16 September 1952)<ref name="cv">{{Cite web |title=Biography Peter Zoller |url=https://resource.iqoqi.at/staff_db/20241216_PZ_Curriculum-Vitae.pdf |access-date=2025-07-17 |publisher=University of Innsbruck}}</ref> is a theoretical physicist from Austria. He is an [[emeritus professor]] at the [[University of Innsbruck]]<ref name="cv" /> and is known for his pioneering research on [[quantum computing]], [[Quantum simulator|quantum simulation]] and [[quantum communication]].<ref name="wolf prize">{{Cite web |title=Peter Zoller – Wolf Prize Laureate in Physics 2013 |date=11 December 2018 |url=https://wolffund.org.il/peter-zoller/ |access-date=2025-07-17 |publisher=[[Wolf Foundation]]}}</ref>

==Biography==
Peter Zoller studied physics at the [[University of Innsbruck]],<ref name="cv"/> where he received his doctorate in February 1977 with a thesis on the [[Stark effect]]<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Zoller |first=Peter |year=1976 | language=de |title=Der dynamische Starkeffekt in intensiven inkohärenten elektromagnetischen Feldern | location=University of Innsbruck |url=https://bibsearch.uibk.ac.at/AC07527343}}</ref> and then worked as an assistant at the Department of Theoretical Physics. In 1978/79, he was a [[Max Kade]] Fellow with [[Peter Lambropoulos]] at the [[University of Southern California]] and in 1980 he stayed in the group of [[Daniel Frank Walls|Dan Walls]] at the [[University of Waikato]][[Hamilton, New Zealand|, New Zealand]]. In 1981, Zoller handed in his work "Über die lichtstatistische Abhängigkeit resonanter Multiphoton-Prozesse"<ref>{{Cite web|title=Über die lichtstatistische Abhängigkeit resonanter Multiphoton-Prozesse|url=http://search.obvsg.at/primo_library/libweb/action/dlDisplay.do?vid=UIB&docId=UIB_aleph_acc000589817&fn=permalink|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140806164449/http://search.obvsg.at/primo_library/libweb/action/dlDisplay.do?vid=UIB&docId=UIB_aleph_acc000589817&fn=permalink|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 August 2014|publisher=University of Innsbruck|access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> at the University of Innsbruck to become lecturer ([[Venia docendi]]). In 1981/82 and 1988 he was Visiting Fellow at the [[Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics]] (JILA) at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder|University of Colorado]], [[Boulder, Colorado|Boulder]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Peter Zoller|url=https://jila.colorado.edu/people/zoller-0|publisher=JILA|access-date=30 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160203014251/https://jila.colorado.edu/people/zoller-0|archive-date=3 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and 1986 a visiting professor at the [[Paris-Sud 11 University|Université de Paris-Sud 11]], [[Orsay]].

In 1991, Zoller became Professor at the Physics Department of the University of Colorado, Boulder, and JILA Fellow. At the end of 1994, he accepted a chair at the University of Innsbruck, where he worked until 2024. From 1995 to 1999, he headed the Department of Theoretical Physics, from 2001 to 2004, he was vice-dean of studies. From 2003 to 2024, he was a Scientific Director at the [[Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information]] (IQOQI) of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information |url=http://iqoqi.at/en |access-date=30 July 2014 |publisher=IQOQI}}</ref>

Zoller remained closely associated with JILA as an Adjoint Fellow. Numerous guest professorships have taken him to major centers of physics. Among others, he was Loeb Lecturer at [[Harvard University]] (2004)<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Boston Area Physics Calendar|url=https://www.het.brown.edu/seminars/bapc/old.bapc/fall-spring-04.txt/2.16.04.txt|publisher=Brown University|access-date=30 July 2014|archive-date=10 August (2005)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lorentz Chair|url=http://www.lorentz.leidenuniv.nl/lorentzchair/|publisher=Leiden University|access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> and Distinguished Lecturer at the [[Technion]] in [[Haifa]] (2007).<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Lewiner Institute for Theoretical Physics Distinguished Lecture |website=Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (CSIC)}}</ref>

In 2018, Peter Zoller co-founded [[Alpine Quantum Technologies]], a [[quantum computing]] hardware company.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://investinaustria.at/en/news/2018/03/quantum-computer.php |title = Austria promotes quantum computing spin-off|publisher=Invest in Austria|date=March 7, 2018}}</ref> As a member of the ''Quantum Computing Advisory Board'' he is advicing the [[European Commission]] on the state of quantum computing in Europe.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-28 |title=New Quantum Computing Advisory Board launched to support the European Commission |url=https://qt.eu/news/2026/2026-04-28_New_Quantum_Computing_Advisory_Board_launched_to_support_the_European-Commission |access-date=2026-08-03 |website=Quantum Flagship |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

==Research==
As a theoretical physicist, Zoller has made significant contributions to [[atomic physics]], [[many-body physics]] and [[quantum information science]]. In particular, his proposals on quantum computing with [[Ion trap|trapped ions]], on quantum simulation with [[ultracold atom]]s in [[optical lattice]]s and on [[quantum repeater]]s in quantum communication have made a decisive contribution to bringing theoretical concepts of quantum information into a laboratory setting. This has inspired and  guided new experimental research directions and established quantum optical systems as one of the leading experimental platforms for quantum technologies.

In 1995, together with [[Ignacio Cirac]], he proposed a “quantum computer with cold trapped ions”.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cirac |first1=J. I. |last2=Zoller |first2=P. |date=1995-05-15 |title=Quantum Computations with Cold Trapped Ions |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=74 |issue=20 |pages=4091–4094 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.4091 |pmid=10058410 |bibcode=1995PhRvL..74.4091C |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This was the first experimentally realistic and comprehensive proposal for a universal quantum computer. This work triggered a rapid experimental development in which numerous pioneering achievements such as the demonstration of quantum algorithms, digital quantum simulations, quantum error correction and quantum metrology were achieved. In 1999, Cirac and Zoller proposed a quantum computer based on cold atoms in optical lattices, in which two-qubit gates are executed by controlled collisions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jaksch |first1=D. |last2=Briegel |first2=H.-J. |last3=Cirac |first3=J. I. |last4=Gardiner |first4=C. W. |last5=Zoller |first5=P. |date=1999-03-01 |title=Entanglement of Atoms via Cold Controlled Collisions |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.82.1975 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=82 |issue=9 |pages=1975–1978 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.82.1975 |issn=0031-9007|arxiv=quant-ph/9810087 |bibcode=1999PhRvL..82.1975J }}</ref> A year later, together with [[Mikhail Lukin]] and others, they presented an alternative way to implement these gates using Rydberg atoms.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jaksch |first1=D. |last2=Cirac |first2=J. I. |last3=Zoller |first3=P. |last4=Rolston |first4=S. L. |last5=Côté |first5=R. |last6=Lukin |first6=M. D. |date=2000-09-04 |title=Fast Quantum Gates for Neutral Atoms |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.2208 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=85 |issue=10 |pages=2208–2211 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.2208 |issn=0031-9007|arxiv=quant-ph/0004038 |bibcode=2000PhRvL..85.2208J }}</ref> With the ever-improving experimental control of neutral atoms in [[Optical tweezers|laser tweezers]], this approach is becoming increasingly important.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bluvstein |first1=Dolev |last2=Evered |first2=Simon J. |last3=Geim |first3=Alexandra A. |last4=Li |first4=Sophie H. |last5=Zhou |first5=Hengyun |last6=Manovitz |first6=Tom |last7=Ebadi |first7=Sepehr |last8=Cain |first8=Madelyn |last9=Kalinowski |first9=Marcin |last10=Hangleiter |first10=Dominik |last11=Bonilla Ataides |first11=J. Pablo |last12=Maskara |first12=Nishad |last13=Cong |first13=Iris |last14=Gao |first14=Xun |last15=Sales Rodriguez |first15=Pedro |date=2024-02-01 |title=Logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=626 |issue=7997 |pages=58–65 |doi=10.1038/s41586-023-06927-3 |pmid=38056497 |issn=0028-0836 |pmc=10830422 |arxiv=2312.03982 |bibcode=2024Natur.626...58B }}</ref>

In 1998, Cirac and Zoller proposed the use of ultracold atoms in optical lattices as an analog quantum simulator for [[Hubbard model]]s to investigate questions in [[solid-state physics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jaksch |first1=D. |last2=Bruder |first2=C. |last3=Cirac |first3=J. I. |last4=Gardiner |first4=C. W. |last5=Zoller |first5=P. |date=1998-10-12 |title=Cold Bosonic Atoms in Optical Lattices |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.3108 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=81 |issue=15 |pages=3108–3111 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.3108|arxiv=cond-mat/9805329 |bibcode=1998PhRvL..81.3108J }}</ref> This approach allows strongly interacting many-body systems to be probed in both equilibrium and non-equilibrium states, addressing key questions in the theory and design of correlated quantum materials and in regimes challenging for classical calculations.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cirac |first1=Ignacio |last2=Zoller |first2=Peter |year=2012 |title=Goals and opportunities in quantum simulation |journal=Nature Physics |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=8 |issue=4 |pages=264–266 |bibcode=2012NatPh...8..264C |doi=10.1038/nphys2275 |s2cid=109930964}}</ref> The experimental development of this platform has led to a number of important advances, including the first observation of the transition between [[superfluidity]] and a [[Mott insulator]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Greiner |first1=Markus |last2=Mandel |first2=Olaf |last3=Esslinger |first3=Tilman |last4=Hänsch |first4=Theodor W. |last5=Bloch |first5=Immanuel |date=2002-01-03 |title=Quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator in a gas of ultracold atoms |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/415039a |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=415 |issue=6867 |pages=39–44 |doi=10.1038/415039a |pmid=11780110 |issn=0028-0836|arxiv=2506.21303 |bibcode=2002Natur.415...39G }}</ref> the creation and study of [[Topological phases of matter|topological quantum phases of matter]] with synthetic [[gauge field]]s, and the exploration of the 2D fermionic Hubbard model.

Also in 1998, a team led by Zoller presented the concept of quantum repeaters,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Briegel |first1=H.-J. |last2=Dür |first2=W. |last3=Cirac |first3=J. I. |last4=Zoller |first4=P. |date=1998-12-28 |title=Quantum Repeaters: The Role of Imperfect Local Operations in Quantum Communication |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.5932 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=81 |issue=26 |pages=5932–5935 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.5932 |bibcode=1998PhRvL..81.5932B |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription |arxiv=quant-ph/9803056 }}</ref> which overcame the problems associated with noise and the loss of photons in optical fibers and made quantum communication over long distances possible. Previously, they had discovered the possibility of entangling atoms by exchanging photons at a distance.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Van Enk |first1=S. J. |last2=Cirac |first2=J. I. |last3=Zoller |first3=P. |last4=Kimble |first4=H. J. |last5=Mabuchi |first5=H. |date=1997-10-01 |title=Quantum state transfer in a quantum network: A quantum-optical implementation |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/09500349708231842 |journal=Journal of Modern Optics |language=en |volume=44 |issue=10 |pages=1727–1736 |doi=10.1080/09500349708231842 |bibcode=1997JMOp...44.1727V |issn=0950-0340|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2001, they proposed a specific atomic setup to build such quantum repeaters.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duan |first1=L.-M. |last2=Lukin |first2=M. D. |last3=Cirac |first3=J. I. |last4=Zoller |first4=P. |date=2001-11-22 |title=Long-distance quantum communication with atomic ensembles and linear optics |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/35106500 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=414 |issue=6862 |pages=413–418 |doi=10.1038/35106500 |pmid=11719796 |issn=0028-0836|arxiv=quant-ph/0105105 |bibcode=2001Natur.414..413D }}</ref> These have become a crucial building block for the development and deployment of quantum communication.

Zoller's ideas and concepts attract widespread interest within the scientific community and his works are highly cited.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Peter Zoller |url=https://www.webofscience.com/wos/author/record/O-1639-2014 |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Web of Science |publisher=Clarivate}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Google Scholar Citations|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=iKB_xp0AAAAJ&hl=en|publisher=Google Scholar|access-date=10 April 2014}}</ref>

==Awards==
Peter Zoller received [[honorary doctorate]]s of the [[University of Amsterdam]] (2012),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorary doctorate for Prof. Peter Zoller |url=http://iop.uva.nl/news-events/content/2011/11/honorary-doctorate-for-prof-peter-zoller.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219023644/http://iop.uva.nl/news-events/content/2011/11/honorary-doctorate-for-prof-peter-zoller.html |archive-date=19 December 2013 |access-date=10 April 2014 |publisher=University of Amsterdam}}</ref> the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] (2019),<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 April 2019 |title=Everything you need to know about the May 9 commencement ceremon |url=https://www.colorado.edu/today/2019/04/30/everything-you-need-know-about-may-9-commencement-ceremony |access-date=9 May 2019 |publisher=University of Colorado Boulder}}</ref> and the [[University of Concepción]] (2024).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-05 |title=UdeC inviste como Doctor Honoris Causa al físico austríaco Dr. Peter Zoller |url=https://noticias.udec.cl/udec-inviste-como-doctor-honoris-causa-al-fisico-austriaco-dr-peter-zoller/ |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=Noticias UdeC |language=es}}</ref>

For his achievements in the field of quantum optics and quantum information and especially for his pioneering work on quantum computers, quantum simulation and quantum communication he als received numerous prizes, these include:

* [[Wittgenstein Award]] (1998), Austria's highest scientific distinction<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wittgenstein Award Laureate 1998 Univ. Prof. Dr. Peter Zoller |url=http://www.wittgenstein-club.at/1998Zoller-en.htm |access-date=10 April 2014 |publisher=Wittgensteinpreis TrägerInnen Club}}</ref>

Zoller|url=http://www.oeaw.ac.at/english/about/personen/mitarbeiter/detail-page.html?user_oeawperssuche_pi1%5bid%5d=11002|publisher=Austrian Academy of Sciences|access-date=10 April == Books ==
Peter Zoller and [[Crispin Gardiner]] have jointly written:
* ''Quantum Noise'';  Springer, Berlin Heidelberg, 2nd ed. 1999, 3rd ed. 2004 {{isbn|3540223010}}
* ''The Quantum World of Ultra-Cold Atoms and Light Book I:  Foundations of Quantum Optics'', Imperial College Press, London and Singapore 2014. {{isbn|9781783264605}}
* ''The Quantum World of Ultra-Cold Atoms and Light Book II:  Physics of Quantum Optical Devices'', Imperial College Press, London and Singapore 2015. {{isbn|9781783266166}}
* ''The Quantum World of Ultra-Cold Atoms and Light Book III:  Ultra-Cold Atoms'', World Scientific, London and Singapore 2014. {{isbn|9781786344175}}
